item.title: Full SQL Tutorial - Beginners
item.description: Start Point of SQL SQL Syntax SELECT Statement The SELECT statement is used when retrieving data selectively from a database. The selected data is usually returned in a table format, commonly referred to as a result set. The basic syntax for the SELECT statement is as follows: SELECT <field_name> FROM <table_name> Using * retrieves data from all fields, or you can specify field names to fetch data from specific fields.

item.title: Learn SQL Select: with Examples
item.description: SQL - SELECT The SELECT statement is used to retrieve data from a database. The returned data is stored in a table-like structure called a result set. SELECT Syntax SELECT column1, column2, ... FROM table_name; Here, column1, column2, … are the field names of the table from which you want to select data. To select all available fields in a table, you can use the following syntax: SELECT * FROM table_name; Demo Database Columns are separated by commas, and the order matters as specified.

item.title: SQL - DELETE Statement
item.description: SQL - DELETE Statement The DELETE statement is utilized to remove existing records from a table. DELETE Syntax DELETE FROM table_name WHERE condition; Note: Exercise caution when deleting records from a table! Be sure to review the WHERE clause of the DELETE statement. The WHERE clause specifies which records will be deleted. Omitting the WHERE clause will result in the deletion of all records from the table! item.title: SQL Aggregate Functions: COUNT(), AVG(), SUM()
item.description: SQL Aggregate Functions: COUNT(), AVG(), SUM() The SQL COUNT(), AVG(), and SUM() functions are essential tools for aggregating and summarizing data in a database. COUNT() Function The COUNT() function calculates the number of rows that meet a specified condition. COUNT() Syntax SELECT COUNT(column_name) FROM table_name WHERE condition; COUNT() Example Consider the following SQL query, which counts the number of products: SELECT COUNT(ProductID) FROM Products; This query returns the total count of products in the database.

item.title: SQL ANY and ALL Operators - with Examples
item.description: SQL ANY and ALL Operators The SQL ANY and ALL operators are commonly used with the WHERE or HAVING clauses in SQL queries. ANY Operator The ANY operator returns True if any of the values in the subquery satisfy the specified condition. The syntax for the ANY operator is as follows: SELECT column_name(s) FROM table_name WHERE column_name operator ANY (SELECT column_name FROM table_name WHERE condition); Note: The operator must be a standard comparison operator (=, <>, !

item.title: SQL HAVING Clause: Examples and Syntax
item.description: SQL - HAVING In SQL, the HAVING clause is introduced to complement the WHERE keyword when working with aggregate functions. HAVING Syntax SELECT column_name(s) FROM table_name WHERE condition GROUP BY column_name(s) HAVING condition ORDER BY column_name(s); Demo Database SQL HAVING Examples Consider the following SQL query, which lists the number of customers in each country, including only countries with more than 5 customers: SELECT COUNT(CustomerID), Country FROM Customers GROUP BY Country HAVING COUNT(CustomerID) > 5; The next SQL query lists the number of customers in each country, sorted in descending order of customer count (including only countries with more than 5 customers).

item.title: SQL ORDER BY Keyword - With Examples
item.description: SQL - ORDER BY Keyword The ORDER BY keyword is employed to sort the result set in ascending or descending order. By default, the ORDER BY keyword arranges records in ascending order. To sort records in descending order, use the DESC keyword. ORDER BY Syntax SELECT column1, column2, ... FROM table_name ORDER BY column1, column2, ... ASC|DESC; ORDER BY Example SELECT * FROM Customers ORDER BY Country; ORDER BY DESC Example Appending DESC at the end sorts the data in descending order.

item.title: SQL Queries: Learn TOP, LIMIT, and ROWNUM in SQL
item.description: SQL - TOP, LIMIT, ROWNUM In SQL, the SELECT TOP clause is used to specify the number of records to return. The SELECT TOP clause proves useful when dealing with large tables that contain thousands of records. Returning a large number of records can impact performance. Note: It’s important to be aware that not all database systems support the SELECT TOP clause. For instance, MySQL uses the LIMIT clause to select a limited number of records, while Oracle employs ROWNUM.

item.title: SQL SELECT INTO Statement - With Examples
item.description: SQL SELECT INTO Statement The SQL SELECT INTO statement is employed to copy data from one table into a new table. SQL SELECT INTO Syntax Copy all columns into a new table: SELECT * INTO newtable [IN externaldb] FROM oldtable WHERE condition; Copy specific columns into a new table: SELECT column1, column2, column3, ... INTO newtable [IN externaldb] FROM oldtable WHERE condition; The new table is created with column names and types as defined in the original table.

item.title: SQL UPDATE Statement - With Examples
item.description: Learn SQL: Usage of the UPDATE Statement The UPDATE statement in SQL allows for the modification of existing records within a table, offering a powerful tool for data manipulation. Key Concepts UPDATE Syntax UPDATE table_name SET column1 = value1, column2 = value2, ... WHERE condition; Note: Exercise caution when using the UPDATE statement to avoid unintended updates. Always include a WHERE clause to specify the records to be updated. Omitting the WHERE clause will result in updating all records in the table.

item.title: Tutorial SQL EXISTS Operator
item.description: SQL EXISTS Operator The SQL EXISTS operator is utilized to test the existence of records in a subquery. EXISTS Syntax SELECT column_name(s) FROM table_name WHERE EXISTS (SELECT column_name FROM table_name WHERE condition); Demo Database SQL EXISTS Examples The following SQL query returns TRUE and lists suppliers with products priced below 20. SELECT SupplierName FROM Suppliers WHERE EXISTS (SELECT ProductName FROM Products WHERE SupplierId = Suppliers.supplierId AND Price < 20); The next SQL query returns TRUE and lists suppliers with products priced at 22.

item.title: Tutorial SQL IN Operator Explained
item.description: SQL - IN Operator: Simplifying Multiple Conditions The SQL IN operator allows the specification of multiple values in the WHERE clause, providing a concise alternative to multiple OR conditions. item.title: Tutorial SQL MIN() and MAX() Functions
item.description: Exploring SQL MIN() and MAX() Functions The SQL MIN() and MAX() functions are powerful tools for finding the smallest and largest values in a selected column, respectively. Understanding MIN() Function The MIN() function retrieves the smallest value in the specified column. MIN() Syntax SELECT MIN(column_name) FROM table_name WHERE condition; MIN() Example Consider the following SQL query to find the price of the most affordable product: SELECT MIN(Price) AS SmallestPrice FROM Products; This returns the smallest price from the “Products” table.

The order of columns in each SELECT statement must align. item.title: Understanding SQL NULL Values
item.description: SQL NULL Values In SQL, NULL represents the absence of a value in a field. When a field in a table is optional, you can insert a new record or update an existing one without providing a value for that field, and the field will be stored as NULL. Note: It’s essential to understand that a NULL value is different from a field with a value of 0 or an empty string.

item.title: What is Trigger in SQL? 2023
item.description: Trigger is a special type of stored procedure that is executed automatically in response to certain events on a database table Triggers are used to enforce business rules, maintain data integrity, and perform tasks such as auditing. Triggers can be activated by various events, such as INSERT , UPDATE , DELETE , or SELECT statements on a table, or by direct invocation using the EXECUTE or CALL statement. Triggers can also be activated by database events such as logon, logoff, or server startup.

item.description: As a data analyst looking to improve your skills, you may be interested in learning SQL, a programming language used for managing and manipulating data stored in relational databases. There are multiple SQL languages available, so you may be wondering which SQL database would be the best option to start learning SQL. List of SQL databases to start learning - open source There are many open source SQL databases that you can start learning.
